newsitem.title: SPAIN: Naomi Campbell leaves Canaries after health scare.
newsitem.headline: Naomi Campbell leaves Canaries after health scare.

text.p: British supermodel Naomi Campbell was discharged from a hospital in the Canary Islands late on Sunday and flew to Paris after receiving emergency treatment for what a hospital official described as a drug overdose.
The 26-year-old model's lawyers denied she had overdosed and insisted she had been rushed to hospital after an allergic reaction to antibiotics.

Officials at the hospital on the Spanish island of Gran Canaria said the model was treated in the intensive care unit in the early hours of Sunday, but had made a steady recovery and was released on Sunday evening.
"Naomi Campbell was discharged from the hospital shortly after 10.00 p.m. (2000 GMT)," a nurse told Reuters.
Campbell left the hospital through a rear exit and went to Las Palmas airport where officials said she chartered a private aircraft and flew to Paris.

A hospital official earlier said that Campbell had been admitted into intensive care after some kind of "overdose". The hospital would not reveal further details of Campbell's condition, but local media reported that she had taken sedatives.
However, a spokesman for Campbell, Jonathan Goldstein of law firm Olswang, ruled out any kind of overdose.
"Ms Campbell is perfectly well and fully recovered and will be leaving hospital later today," Olswang said earlier on Sunday.
"She wishes to make it clear that there is absolutely no foundation whatsoever to the story that she had taken an overdose," he said in a statement issued to Britain's Press Association news agency.
Local media reported that Campbell had arrived on the island on Friday on the same plane as her boyfriend, 28-year-old flamenco dancer Joaquin Cortes.
At around 0200 GMT on Sunday she was taken semi-conscious from her five-star hotel in the island capital Las Palmas to the Nuestra Senora del Pino hospital, officials said.
Local media said the catwalk model had earlier had an argument with Cortes, who is in Gran Canaria with his hugely successful "Gypsy Passion" dance show.
Residents at the luxury hotel, where Campbell and Cortes had been staying in separate rooms, were reported to have complained about a heated conversation between the two.
Hotel staff said Campbell had appeared extremely nervous after the discussion and had taken some form of medicine, local media reported. The hotel would not comment on the reports.
Dressed in his trademark black, Cortes arrived at the hospital on Sunday afternoon to visit the supermodel, who commands tens of thousands of dollars for a morning's work.
He spent several hours at the hospital and later left to star in his hit show at a local theatre.

After being discharged, local media reported that Campbell left the hospital by a kitchen exit and was driven away in a Mercedes-Benz car to the airport. Photographers saw her smiling and chatting with her companions wearing a lime green jumper and sunglasses as she waited to leave the island.
Airport officials said the supermodel chartered a private plane which took off at 2335 GMT, heading for Le Bourget airport on the outskirts of Paris.
Campbell has been linked for several months to Cortes, the long-haired flamenco star who is dubbed "sex on legs" for his steamy dancing.
But gossip magazines recently reported that the Spanish dancer had broken up with Campbell and was pictured with another woman on holiday in the southern resort of Marbella.
His "Gypsy Passion" show is thrilling audiences across Europe and North America with erotic dancing which blends flamenco, ballet and jazz.
